top_story: Since Trump’s March threat to destroy Iran’s power plants unless Tehran reopens the Strait of Hormuz, Tehran has framed confrontation as both external deterrence and internal discipline, warning of regional escalation while intensifying repression at home. That domestic hardening is visible in the latest execution of another protester on 25 May, part of a broader wave of hangings on political and security charges that leaves dozens more at risk and deepens public fear. In Lebanon, Israel’s alleged killing of more than 120 paramedics and rescue workers since 2 March has eroded already fragile civilian protection and widened the human costs of cross-border conflict. The regional picture is one of escalating coercion by state actors, where military signaling abroad and punitive violence against civilians and dissenters reinforce instability rather than contain it.
